title: Depression-era jobs in Buras
summary: After 1930 he played many jobs in Buras and Venice, where clubs had no names.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Can you remember any other jobs you had during the Depression, after 1930, along in there? After you closed out at the lake, at Millenburg?
I played several different jobs, I mean. It's hard to think of them, played so many of them. I went down to Buress a long time.
All through your career, yeah. What played you played at Buress most? Huh? I played Buress, Venus. I mean, who you played for at Buress most? Rex Club or Buck Jones or?

I know the name, all I know where they was. I mean, I never knew their name. See, none of them fellas, people didn't carry no name at their club at that time like they do now, you know. All they tell you they got a job in Buress, I mean, they put no name on no contract or nothing. They tell you Buress, I mean. I went down there so long, I just couldn't know where it was by heart, I mean. There was no other place to play, it was better than Chauvin. Yeah. They had a funny name there, yeah. Funny name they called them, I mean. A long time ago, they never had no name, I mean, like they got now, I mean, like the Star Club and all that, like they got all out there. They didn't, they didn't had that.
Well, whoever is going to play, I said, where are you going? I'm going to play for Mr. Soil.

Yeah. Felice, come on, Felice, Felice was in Buress, I mean, that's, you know, that was going to play for him. John Rowell, I mean, at Sunrise, you know. It was just, say the name who was going to play for it, so people would know.
